subject: maths
source_note: Topic structure follows the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics (Spec A) specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

connections.why: Fractions extend the four rules of arithmetic to non-integer quantities
Fractions, decimals and percentages are interchangeable forms of the same value
A percentage is a fraction out of 100, so percentage work builds on fractions
Prime factorisation and index laws generalise multiplication of integers
Standard form relies on powers of ten and index laws
Ratio notation is closely linked to fractions and division of quantities
Algebra generalises the rules of arithmetic using symbols for numbers
Manipulating expressions depends on understanding symbols and index laws
Factorising and completing the square are tools for solving quadratics
Rearranging formulae uses the same manipulation skills as simplifying expressions
Simultaneous equations combine and solve pairs of linear equations
Algebraic proportion formalises numerical ratio and proportion as equations
Straight-line graphs y = mx + c are the visual form of linear equations
Roots of a quadratic are where its graph crosses the x-axis
Differentiation finds the gradient and turning points of a curve's graph
Functions are represented and analysed through their graphs
Polygon angle sums are derived from the angle properties of triangles
Angle facts provide the statements used to justify geometric reasoning
Circle theorems supply reasons for angle calculations in circles
Pythagoras' theorem and surd answers depend on squares and roots
Sine and cosine functions are plotted as trigonometric graphs
Surface areas of solids are built from the 2D areas of their faces
Similar figures have corresponding lengths in a fixed ratio
Translations are described by column vectors, linking the two topics
Graph transformations parallel geometric reflections, translations and stretches
Probabilities are calculated and combined as fractions
Venn diagrams and sample spaces use set notation to find probabilities
Plotting and reading axes underpins statistical diagrams
